Diese Folge schildert, wie sich auf dem vielgestaltigen kleinen Kontinent erstmals ein europäischer Kulturraum entwickelte: Die ersten Menschen wanderten aus Afrika ein, später entstanden Volksgruppen wie die Kelten, Staatengebilde wie Griechenland und das Imperium der Römer, das weite Teile Europas umfasste und verband. Bis heute ist Europa ein Schauplatz vielfältiger Migration geblieben. Der Historiker Christopher Clark beleuchtet die Entstehung des europäischen Kulturraums.

Der christliche Glaube spielt eine zentrale Rolle für die Identität Europas, das als "christliches Abendland" gilt. Kirchengemeinden und Klöster wurden zur Keimzelle gemeinsamer Konfession, Pilgerwege zu einem verbindenden europäischen Netzwerk. Doch die Christen im Osten und Westen Europas gingen bald schon getrennte Wege. Der Islam prägte in al-Andalus über ein halbes Jahrtausend die Kultur im westlichen Europa mit, und auch die Juden trugen zur kulturellen Vielfalt Europas bei.

Diese Folge erzählt die Geschichte der europäischen Expansion von der Zeit der Wikinger bis zum Britischen Weltreich. Europa und die Welt, das ist eine Historie von Entdeckergeist und Unternehmertum, aber auch von Imperialismus, Unterdrückung und Ausbeutung. Christopher Clark führt die Zuschauer an Ausgangspunkte des Aufbruchs, wie Lissabon, Amsterdam und London, und beleuchtet die Gründe dafür, dass es Europäer immer wieder in die Weite gezogen hat.

Dieses Mal geht es um Europas Beitrag zur Weltkultur. Christopher Clark reist in die europäischen Metropolen, um sich Kunst, Unterhaltung, Philosophie und Wissenschaft zu widmen, die ohne Rücksicht geschaffen wurden.

Erfahren Sie mehr über den Weg Europas zur Einheit. Dabei hatte nicht immer die Vernunft Vorrang: Oft wurde auch Gewalt angewandt, um Mitstreiter zu unterwerfen und zu beherrschen. Christopher Clark betrachtet die Geschichte genauer.

Brexit, Finanzkrisen und Flüchtlingswellen haben in Europa Skepsis und nationale Rückbesinnung an die Stelle früherer Aufbruchstimmung rücken lassen. Doch es gibt auch Optimismus. Europa hat gemeinsam Dinge erzielt, von denen die Gründer nur zu träumen wagten: das Ende des Kalten Krieges, die Öffnung nach Osten, eine einheitliche Währung. Und trotz mehrerer Krisen und Konfliktherde gibt es das Europa der gemeinsamen Kultur und des selbstverständlichen Austausches.

Die 537 eingeweihte Basilika Hagia Sophia in Istanbul ist ein architektonisches Meisterwerk mit wechselvoller Geschichte. Eintausend Jahre lang war sie die größte Kirche der Welt und das religiöse und symbolische Zentrum des ersten großen christlichen Reiches. Bis zur Eroberung Konstantinopels war die Hagia Sophia das größte Gotteshaus der Christenheit. Nach der Eroberung Konstantinopels 1453 wandelten sie die Osmanen in eine Moschee um und fügten als äußeres Kennzeichen vier Minarette hinzu.

Gumball and Darwin flood the house; Gumball goes to school in a dress and becomes the darling of Elmore High; Gumball and Darwin challenge Dad to a lazy-off; Gumball must learn to say no when Carrie the Ghost uses his body against his will.

Join the CBBC crew for all your favourite programmes. Tune into CBBC every day from 7.00am.

It's breakfast time and The Farmer discovers he has no fresh milk for his morning cup of tea. He sets off in great haste, only to become ensnared in a 'rush hour' traffic jam. Shaun and The Flock are too impatient to wait for breakfast and take matters into their own hands.

Stuff is going missing all over the world, but the team are distracted, fascinated by Squawk's new Futuroid camera, which incredibly spits out snaps of future events. When Penfold is abducted by an alien tractor-beam Squawk and Danger Mouse must overcome their mutual disgust to work together. Their search for Penfold leads them to Flarg, the alien who's been nabbing the world's missing items.
Mr Friendlyface accompanies the heroes on a quest and makes everything worse by angering a Big Ole Worm, putting all their lives in danger.

Suddenly feeling too old to be collecting toys, Boy gives up his bobbleheads and replaces this activity by doing a bunch of things he imagines true grown-ups do. Unfortunately, he goes over-the-top and the occasionally fun Boy now becomes an old Man.
News magazine keeping young viewers up to date with the latest stories and events happening at home and abroad.

The lemmings break Grizzy's sand statues. Furious, the bear sends them far away to build a huge statue in peace. But when he wants to take a photo next to his work, the lemmings attack with a pirate cannon.
The lemmings are hypnotised by a poster and suddenly think they are fitness trainers. They want to force Grizzy to work out, but he would rather continue to lie around than do push-ups and squats.
SpongeBob helps out the Krusty Krab's night shift crew, but the customers crave something creepier than usual.
While operating a lift, Duck and Frog cause mayhem for the Mayor's grand opening.
Duck soon learns that he is a terrible babysitter, but it seems kids love Frog!
Osric is followed by a documentary crew.
Experience the ultimate in long-distance travel - a holiday on Mars!
A lesson on how to cope with change.

It's estimated that as many as 250 million sharks are taken from the world's oceans every single year. Around 73 million of those are taken purely for their fins which are used in shark fin soup, with the rest of the body wasted.

All the top sporting action from the past, including Emperor Nero and Jesse Owens singing the history of the Olympics. We're at the finish line to see Pheidippides run the first ever marathon, then we count down the top Marathon Cheats of all time and take a look back at some of our favourite Horrible Histories sporting events.

Gannets prove to be more than a match for Steve in a diving competition. He then has to confront his past as he comes face-to-face with the only venomous snake that has hospitalised him. The Deadly team also have a close call as they uncover a hornets' nest in a loft, and Steve gets a taste of what it is like to be prey for a day as he is hunted through a forest by a hungry goshawk.

The doctors choose some of their favourite moments, including an experiment to find out what happens when you cough and a life-changing operation that allows someone to hear for the very first time. There's a brand new mind-bending trick to baffle your brain, and the ouch-mobile opens its doors to help solve more medical mysteries.
Buddy and boxer Jackson take a time-out to make a fish finger sarnie that packs a punch.

Dr Chris and Dr Xand van Tulleken meet the top experts on the planet to demonstrate things that will blow your mind. They find out about brainy birds. Chris Packham visits a safe-cracking parrot called Muppet, a watch-stealing cockatoo called Olympia and even some time-travelling birds.
Joe and Meryl take a look back at some of the fun moments and amazing dens from the series.
At the sanctuary, the brothers and big cats are celebrating Chinese New Year. Some tasty Chinese lanterns help Luka the Amur leopard break the ice with his neighbour Xizi.
As the girls celebrate Chinese New Year, PE teacher Miss Elsley believes netball player Jina could be destined for sporting success. She's arranged a visit from a local scout.

Oskar tries to balance exam revision with time at the track. He may not have trained as much as he'd have liked but hopes he can make it count at this week's big race event. Newbie Freya goes in her second ever race after a bad fall.

After Shellington crashes the Gup-D, he teams up with Kwazii, a moray eel and grouper fish to pick up the pieces.

The Piripenguins fall under the spell of a magical Merguin, a mermaid-penguin, who has the ability to change their personality. But all is not as it seems.
It's a smelly disaster for Wizz. The more people watch, the more everything around him starts to stink.
Duck's has to sneak into a greenhouse to get his plant back after it is mistakenly sold.

When the kids get hold of an old ice cream truck, they start their own smoothie business! But the town's lovable ice cream man - Uncle Bub - isn't happy to have competition. He sets out to sabotage our heroes and keep them from serving.
The Comets are physically ready to run their first full-out, but emotions run high as Jax realises he has feelings for Olive. Meanwhile, Ruby struggles to keep Melody's plan a secret.

Naturalist Steve Backshall is headed to the Bahamas in order to get up close and personal with a whole bunch of sharks. There are plenty of shark species to choose from and Steve has his work cut out deciding which ones are worthy of a place on his `Deadly 60' list.

Shaun steals whistles from Bitzer that can control the herd's movements. He then makes the sheep dance to his music. When the farmer discovers the whistles, Shaun finds himself caught in his own game.
Deep in the caverns below Beanotown Hall, a mysterious species of oversized hamsters may or may not exist, so may or may not be at risk of being hunted down and turned into fluffy slippers.
When an old enemy returns, Colonel K must come out of retirement to save the world from an outbreak of rudeness.
Twinkle feels she is being taken for granted by the other heroes, so she joins the Fairy Squad when they arrive.

With the rest of the gang sick with colds, Mouse builds himself his own personal transparent bubble to keep himself healthy. But soon the others also get their bubbles to enjoy their own space, even if they're not sick any more.
Grizzy starts a school to teach the wild Lemmings some discipline, but he has forgotten that they naturally love chaos.

When Eoin shows Pablo funny videos of a boy called Evan Stephens, Pablo decides to try to be cool and get likes by copying the influencer - with disastrous results!
The kids find a mysterious egg inside Arthur's plane and decide to hatch it.

Kenzie and the Comets face off against Coach Cutler and the Cheery Bombs at Cheermageddon.
Live from the Roots and Fruits theatre, it's Carrot performing a superstylish song, if he manages to make up his mind and pick an outfit.
Bing makes Sula a picture with all her favourite things on it. It just needs one last jewel to be stuck on, but the glue spills all over the picture. Sparkles save the day.
It is a windy day in Teletubbyland and Dipsy's hat blows away, but Po helps Dipsy to get his hat back. In Tummy Tales, children have fun playing on a windy beach.
Tee and Mo are having a dancing day! That is, until Tee notices someone laughing at them. Can Mo get Tee to dance like no-one's watching again?
Imaginative Purple arrives in Colourland. Learn about the colour purple with the Colourblocks.
Dad retells the story of the three little pigs. However, the pigs and the wolf become friends.

Sula and Amma surprise Bing to show him Sula's sparkly painted butterfly face. Bing also wants a painted face, one that looks like Biteysaurus, and Sula says she can do it for him. Preston needs Mojo's racer top speed to get his new plane off the ground. But when his flight goes wrong, Mojo and Bo have to take to the air in Mojo's jet top to help him down!

Duggee masters his ambition of building a model of the Clubhouse out of sticks, so the Squirrels start to think about what their ambitions might be. Norrie wants to learn how to breakdance. Tag spends a long time thinking what his could be, and then it clicks - he needs to climb over the log!

The Squirrels are out walking around in the rain with Duggee and notice a rainbow. But before they know it, it's gone and the Squirrels are devastated. They decide to make their own rainbow and go off in search of all the colours from everything around them, including strawberries, carrots and bananas. Duggee shows the Squirrels what he has been working on too, a rainbow cake.
Bluey and Bingo want Dad to play two different games, so Dad tries to play both at the same time.
Mum, Dad and Bingo must complete both their classes to pass swim school but pleasing strict Big Fish instructor Margaret, aka Bluey, is proving very difficult.

When Glitch crash lands at the Go Jet Academy, he's furious to see that his accident was caused by a flowery plant blocking Grim HQ's chimneys. But Tala loves this plant and plans to grow some of the rare flowers in her research garden. Glitch decides to do the same, setting the Grimbots to create the perfect conditions for the plants to grow. But Tala and Foz soon find out that the plant is actually a superweed which grows so fast that it threatens to overwhelm the island.
When Cotton-tail's birthday cake is stolen and Peter vows to get it back, he finds himself in hot water with a host of angry villains!
The Octonauts expand their exploration beyond the sea and onto land. With new rides and new friends, they are prepared to protect any habitats and animals at risk on land or underwater.

One Hundred is on a mission to explore a mysterious signal coming from the depths of space. With the help of the Times Tables, she makes the signal as strong as possible. Times Tables assembles a team to help them investigate the signal.

Take a trip with Tino the Artistic Mouse high in the sky or on the ocean.

Flop arrives, bringing his sleeping bag and Hoppity so they can all sleep over.

Dee encourages a friend to say 'bag' and we go on a whirlwind word adventure. We see lots of different bags: a big bag, a tiny bag and a shiny bag. There's a sleeping bag, a beeping bag and even a leaping bag! The journey is repeated with some special surprises along the way, and everyone has a boogie when Dee's friend finally succeeds in saying today's word!
When Pete comes over to mend a tap, Tralala finds joy in fixing things around the house.
Following Lionel's advice, Mae and Bee help Marsha the turtle find her talent.
Kiri has to overcome her jealousy when everyone gives Lou presents.
The Twirlywoos watch a pot being made on a potter's wheel and decide to have a go themselves. On the boat, the tea table is in a spin.
Justin's friend teaches him how to make Indian chapattis as part of a family banquet. Meanwhile, Mr Tumble is preparing a Diwali surprise for the rest of his family.
It's time to wake up, but Tinky Winky isn't feeling well. Soon after, Tinky Winky feels better, but now Dipsy, Laa-Laa and Po don't feel well.

Giovanna and Baby Bear welcome babies Evie, Joseph, Luke, Thea, Benjamin, Eliza and their grown-ups to The Baby Club. Parents, carers and their babies at home are invited to join in with all the fun activities too! Inside everyone's bags are blankets which are explored through discovery, play, song and story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to take part by hiding a baby appropriate blanket inside a fabric bag or pillowcase for them to reveal and explore with their baby!
Elsie plays I spy in the museum with her new friend Qasim.
With only minutes to go before the big performance at McGinty's farm, Maddie has to use all her musical skills to convince Gary the Chicken to perform with the other animals.
A dusty, old box makes Rebecca sneeze! Murphy dreams up some make ideas to help reveal what is inside, including a tissue box monster and a flamingo sock puppet.

Raa Raa and the other animals keep slipping up on banana skins that are littering the jungle floor. Together the animals clear up the mess and discover who has been littering the jungle with banana skins.
When Dad is forced to stop playing with the girls to do some work, the girls do everything in their power to keep him playing games with them on the trampoline.

Happy comes across a very questionable-looking puddle which he wants to splash in. When the Squirrels see Happy about to step into the smelly puddle, they question whether he should play in it.

Chantelle visits a local school that has a nature garden, whilst Rory meets an expert on slugs. Chantelle and Rory's fact files help explain all of Lucia's questions. Slugs are superheroes, and they help the planet in their own special way.

Follow Deeya as she celebrates Diwali, the Hindu festival of light. Deeya begins by going to the park with her mum, where she learns how the colours and lights represent the festival. After shopping for something to wear for their big Diwali party, Deeya finds the perfect dress and heads back home. There, she helps her great-grandma to cook some delicious, authentic Indian snacks and decorate the house with lots of lights.
Jen is doing the washing up, but her hands are going wrinkly. Gabby the goalkeeper visits the café, and the two chefs make a power shake to give her an energy boost for her next game of football.
Hearing dog Diesel visits Woofton library to work on Rayane's homework project, which is all about sound. But when their timer goes missing, Diesel needs his super ears to find it.
Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet Bactrian camels and a lynx.
Organist Ashley shows his organ shoes, which help him to play the pedals on the floor.
Loud disco music disrupts Waffle's After School Club experience until George the cat finds a solution for Waffle - dog earmuffs to protect his ears. Time for a doggy disco!
Oona and Baba search for soft bedding for their burrow.

It's the day the geese fly over on their annual migration south. When Sonny reports that geese put on an amazing display if you mimic their calls, the gang look for the right sound to get a response from the geese before they fly past.
Lu is really impressed by her mum's one-handed catch and tries to imitate it at school, but she fails multiple times to catch a ball with one hand while playing with Barnaby and Elodie.
Keith and Rebecca think they've broken Fred's clock and call the Piggy Builders to fix it before Fred finds out. But the repair turns out to be impossible!
When Nine needs a helping hand, he turns into a talented trio of circus blocks, the Three Threes. Learn how to share the number nine into equal parts with the Numberblocks.
H makes a hen, who lays an egg, which rolls away. The 'Alphablocks' hop to it, give chase and discover the egg sat on a wall, about to have a great fall.
Mr Tumble and Fisherman Tumble plan a picnic by the lake, but the food keeps disappearing. Meanwhile, Justin takes his friends to a pond, where they have fun with nets.
Tinky Winky, Dipsy, Laa-Laa and Po run around in circles in the Home Dome. The Noo-noo joins in, and the Teletubbies have fun chasing.
Baby elephant Kipekee is fed up with being small, and Hamza sees wildebeest in the wild.

Maddie is having fun with water. She takes a car through an automatic car wash, to find out how the computer uses sensors to tell the robotic car wash how to wash the car. She makes sure to use a special waterproof camera.

Motorbike rider Grace shows off three extraordinary machines that you can actually live in. Grace goes for a sail in a solar-powered canal boat, shows off the International Space Station and goes for a drive in a motorhome.

It is Diwali, and the class has visitors who tell them about the meaning behind the festival of light. The children have a go at making rangoli with Mrs Hussain and try some Indian sweets. Jessica, Theo, and Alba create diya lamps out of clay.
Kyra and Khloe visit a farm where they meet two beautiful ponies. After a quick grooming, they get to take their new friends out for a ride.
Ginger and the baby Pea-Rexes search for honeysuckle, leaving behind a trail of berries to help find their way back. But when Wasabi eats the trail, they're stranded in the dark.
The Octonauts help a group of algae-eating fish stand up to some aggressive damselfish, who are harming their own reef by over-farming it with algae.
Peter's plan to collect the year's first bluebell for his mother takes an unexpected turn when he finds it on Mr Tod's doorstep.

Brinicle tries to turn the Krispy Krill shack into a top restaurant to impress a secret reviewer, but chef Pancake's cooking proves unpopular, and Looph's plate machine misfires.

Evil Pea approaches Broccoli, requesting lessons in flying, after Broccoli accidentally sends her paper plane into the freezer. Evil Pea does not let Broccoli know that she intends to fly high to take over Tato Tower.

Cap'n Gail's tall tale of a nine-legged octopus in Lake Swoppiton has everyone panicking. But Mojo and Bo wonder: is the story real or is Cap'n Gail up to something?
Take to the skies with Zog, the lovable orange dragon and friends.
Dr Ollie urgently needs to nap, but with PC Plum testing his whistles, and Ava's headphones making things too quiet, the children finally lull him to sleep with a gentle lullaby.
It's Waffle's last day at the Brooklyn-Bells' but he still finds time to upset neighbour Mrs Hobbs. Simon hears Waffle speak. Will he finally agree that the family can keep the special dog?
Rafi's speedy wish leads to silly mix-ups all around the busy supermarket.

JoJo and Gran Gran celebrate Diwali, the festival of light, with their friends Raya and Nirada. It's a very exciting celebration, with lots of yummy food, diyas, music and, of course, lights. Raya teaches JoJo how to make a rangoli. And when Raya doesn't like the loud sounds coming from the fireworks, JoJo has a plan to help her friend.
When Sarah has a cold, Duck helps her enjoy a visit to the doctor.
The cloud has been on holiday in space, but returns freezing cold and snowing, not raining. Tiny comes up with a clever plan to warm the cloud up.
Memo and Baba discover all the amazing things you can do with your breath.
Makka Pakka is washing the ball when his uff-uff is blown away. It falls into Upsy Daisy's bed and she carefully retrieves it and sets off through the garden to return it to Makka Pakka.
Get your twinkling stars ready and sing along with Mr Tumble in 'Twinkle Twinkle Little Star'.

Loretta leaves her husband Nick and refuses to get back together with him. Nick tries to lure Diane away from Sam by presenting her dinner, cake, and music, but she resists. Woody beats Frasier at chess, again.
Carla begins a relationship with Eddie LeBec, a goalie from Quebec who plays hockey for the Boston Bruins. She brings Frasier to a game since he is mourning the loss of his lab-chimpanzee, Bombo.
Carrie thinks Spence is lonely and fixes him up with a girl from work. Though Doug gives him some saucy advice which doesn't go quite to plan.
When they attend a friend's wedding Doug discovers some of Carrie's secrets - and he'll wish he hadn't.
The new neighbours' barking dog keeps Doug and Carrie up all night. Meanwhile, Arthur thinks the comic strip character Charlie Brown is based on him.
Ray's wish list for Christmas includes a little romance with Debra, but she proves to be a difficult gift to unwrap.
Raymond joins his brother and Frank in a Gettysburg Civil War re-enactment in an attempt to bond with his father.
Ray is excited about meeting a distant relative, until it turns out she wants to stay longer than promised.
Frasier is arrested after unwittingly giving a ride to a prostitute. To make matters worse, he must explain the public scandal to his visiting 11-year-old son Frederick.

Frasier plays Cupid when he arranges a supposedly accidental meeting between Martin and Roz's mother, but he finds out that Martin can't stand her just minutes before she's the surprise guest at the Cranes' Super Bowl Party.
Woody's (Woody Harrelson) surprise visit soon wears thin when Frasier realises how little they have in common.

Niles prepares for a Valentine's date at Frasier's flat, until a crease in his trousers escalates into a series of calamities. Frasier spends the evening trying to figure out if he's on a date or a business meeting, while Daphne and Martin wallow in their lack of a significant other.
A 135-year-old Colorado opera house packed with vintage Americana; a fellow picker's junkyard home with items that are a bit pricey.

Graham and Jodie uncover forgotten treasures in their 19th-century Cumbrian mansion. On the Isle of Gigha, Andy and Karen set their sights on a dream kitchen. And in Cheshire, Matt and Charlotte attempt to get their bathroom renovation back on track.
There are fishy goings-on in Orlando, as a journalist reviews the Best of British pub. Sarah helps out at a busy dog-walking business. And Anthony and Michelle restart their catering business.
Colin Murray, Rachel Riley and Susie Dent host, with Reverend Kate Bottley in Dictionary Corner, as contestants race against the clock to pit their wits against vowels, consonants and numbers.

Lee Juggurnauth helps Diane and Nigel find their perfect holiday home in France's Dordogne region. They've dreamt of owning their own place in France for years. With a maximum budget of £180,000, Lee shows them five impressive properties.
In France, a new purchase takes Paul and Yip to a momentous milestone. Mike's restoration of his Spanish mountain village grinds to a halt. And George tackles major structural issues in Sicily.
The B&Bers meet one last time on payment day to clash over cleanliness and spar over sleep scores, before the payments are revealed, and we find out who's won.

Carpet and flooring specialist Chris hopes that his music-inspired nosh will have his guests dancing on the ceiling. The evening gets off to a slow start when the guests are subjected to a passionate lecture on the joys of carpets and vinyl flooring.

Debbie and Martin are looking for a family holiday home near Mojácar on Spain's Costa Almería. Working with a budget of £80k, Ben Hillman shows them five great options, but are any of them perfect enough for Debbie and Martin to put in an offer?
Channel 4's flagship news programme. With sport and weather.

Unreported World reports from Johannesburg, where speaking out against corruption can be a death sentence. Reporter Darshna Soni investigates the business of contract killers who are used to silence whistleblowers.

On glorious Ynys Môn (Anglesey) in Wales, Tina, Steve and their daughter are returning to where Tina and Steve grew up and first met as teenagers. They plan to create a magnificent home of steel, glass and stone on a stunning, windswept plot.

Offering their unmatched satirical insight into current world events, Adam, Josh and Alex are joined by comedian Desiree Burch, actor Harry Shearer and politician Ed Miliband to help dissect the biggest news stories of the week.
Sean Lock presents his blend of surreal yet insightful stand-up comedy, recorded at the Theatre Royal in Margate, in which he airs his mischievous views on parenting, old age, and immigration.
Peppa and her friends are in a playgroup and Mr Bull is building a wind turbine. Madame Gazelle explains everything to the children about wind energy.
Mandy Mouse has a birthday visit to a cheese theme park with Peppa and her friends. Everything in the park is cheese-themed, and Mandy loves cheese.
A shadow on the tent spooks Fluff and threatens to spoil Tweedy's camping plan!
Martin, the migratory bird, returns to camp as a refugee after his home is destroyed by a storm.

Thomas is taking a film crew to a nature reserve in China to make a film about giant pandas. While he is very excited by the prospect of seeing them in the wild, he is not sure what they look like and slows down every time he thinks he sees one.
Trevor leads a group hike to the beaver dam and Pontypandy Mountain, but without using a compass and soon without a map, either.
Peppa and her family are on a caravan adventure; the first stop is the biggest potato in the world; when it starts to get too foggy, they park up for a rest before another busy day.
After Pip and Posy set up a stall with Frankie to sell their modelling clay food creations, the pair try to help their friend feel better when no one chooses the food she made.
Paddington does not have a hobby like all the Browns, but Mrs Brown finds out what Paddington is good at.
The pups spring into action when Digi and Taal's coconut catapult goes out of control.
After Speed Meister builds an unsafe playground, Rubble and crew get creative and build a whole new one with old materials.
Pedro Pony pretends he is a proper cowboy, telling everyone stories in the camp he has set up in the garden.
Bobby Beaver shows the families the beaver dam that his family have been building. Peppa and Suzy are still looking for the magical forest fairies.
When Tim finds Blobert, an old toy, it brings out the monster in him.
A mysterious cloud of gulls descends over Porthole and besieges Ellie's fish taco stall. Stan and Gran jump to the rescue whilst avoiding the poop!
Cap'n Turbot loses his glasses and creates chaos in his path. It's up to the PAW Patrol to save him and his specs.
The Cadets visit Cannon Hall Farm, where they help Farmer Rob take stones out of a miniature donkey's hooves, and join Farmer Emma to build a fun pool and ball pit for the ferrets.

When Mrs Sweep has to deal with an emergency at the supermarket, Milo and his friends take it upon themselves to clean up Queen Mabel's dusty palace. They think the vacuum cleaner might be a quick fix.
Peppa and her friends and family are looking forward to a trip to the seaside where they can make sandcastles, but when they arrive at the beach there is too much snow.

Sabrina buys fake ID cards and loses her magic powers; Other Realm pirates run wild in the Spellman household.
When Ray realises that his kids would rather spend time with their Uncle Robert than with him, he decides to do something about the situation.
Debra can't help but question the solidity of her relationship with Ray after her parents make a shocking announcement.
Ray hits the roof when Frank, who generously offered to paint his son's house, refuses to use the colour Ray wants.
As Ray escorts Ally to a father-daughter dance, he realises how grown up and independent his daughter has become, and recalls the day when she was born.

Karl imagines what life would be like if he had a doppelgänger. Meanwhile, Ricky poses a logic riddle that Karl has difficulty solving and Stephen shares some embarrassing anecdotes from a recent trip to Rio de Janeiro. Entries from Karl's Diary include his difficulty understanding art, why he hates Ricky's cat and when medical science goes too far.

Ricky teaches Karl some facts about animals, Karl offers a misguided theory about evolution, then recounts the latest scientific breakthroughs in medicine, and Stephen reads from Karl's Diary, sharing his thoughts about the Congo, the decline of gadgets and watching films with subtitles.

When Monica's parents clear out her old room to install a gym, they unearth an old video of her and Rachel's first prom night. It's obvious from this that Ross is in love with Rachel and, having told him it will never happen, Rachel changes her mind. Elsewhere, Joey gives Chandler a hideous bracelet as a token of his friendship and is mortally offended to hear Chandler saying how terrible it is.

Among the guests at Monica's party is a handsome and sophisticated doctor, but the only problem is that he's old enough to be her father. Meanwhile, Joey buys a big screen TV and two reclining leather armchairs with the money from his `Days of Our Lives' contract.

Everyone at Monica's dad's birthday party finds it amusing that their middle-aged friend, eye-doctor Richard Burke, is dating a woman in her 20s - until Monica's parents learn that it is their daughter. Meanwhile, Chandler and Joey row over a dirty spoon. Is the flat still big enough for both of them?
With Joey in his new flat, Chandler gets a troublesome new flatmate. Phoebe makes a video for 'Smelly Cat' and Ross and Monica find it nearly impossible to live together.
Ross panics when he sees his son with a Barbie doll, and Chandler's fear of commitment surfaces in his relationship with Janice.

Phoebe's attempts to introduce her visiting half brother Frank Jr to the delights of city life leave him thinking that she works in a brothel. Meanwhile, Ross lists five famous women that he would like to date.

When Janice asks the gang if any of them have ever slept together, the friends flashback three years ago. Phoebe moves out of Monica's apartment, Chandler and Joey become roommates, Monica bumps into Rachel, and Ross learns that Carol is a lesbian.
When Monica buys a new bed from the Mattress King, the wrong one is delivered. Meanwhile, Joey sees Janice kissing her husband, and Rachel's father clashes with Ross.
Chandler and Janice reach a turning point in their relationship, while Monica accidentally injures Ben and tries to hide it from Ross.

On Thanksgiving, the friends form teams and play American football. Ross and Monica relive their sibling rivalry by going head-to-head as opposing team captains. Rachel is upset that Ross didn't choose her for his team, and Joey tries to outwit his foe Chandler. Meanwhile, the turkey is left stewing while the losing team calls for a rematch.
Rachel wonders if she'll ever get another job after she quits Central Perk, Joey's new job selling Christmas trees upsets Phoebe, and Ross accidentally breaks a little girl's leg.
Ross is suspicious about Rachel's possible job offer from a good-looking stranger, while Chandler can't remember which of Joey's many attractive sisters he kissed at a party.

Ross becomes increasingly jealous of Rachel's sexy new colleague, Mark, and gets the wrong end of the stick when he spies on Rachel at her office. Meanwhile, Monica is enamoured with a sexy bus boy who writes love poems for her, and Joey gets himself into trouble by faking his CV in order to get a part in a Broadway musical.

Monica bumps into Richard in a video store, and they decide to work on their friendship, but the more time they spend together, the more sexual their relationship becomes. Meanwhile, Phoebe dates an athlete who unintentionally keeps exposing himself by wearing loose shorts, and Rachel agrees to read 'The Shining' if Joey will read 'Little Women'.

Phoebe is reunited with her former singing partner, Leslie, a failed television commercial jingle writer who wants to use Phoebe's signature song 'Smelly Cat' in an advertisement for cat litter. Meanwhile, Ross becomes jealous when Rachel agrees to go to a fashion lecture with Mark, a former colleague who has just left for a new job, and Chandler meets a beautiful woman, Ginger, who has a prosthetic leg.

Rachel's job prevents her from celebrating her anniversary with Ross. Wanting more time to focus on her new job, she suggests the two take a break from their relationship. Convinced that Rachel has dumped him for one of her workmates, Ross hooks up with a woman from the copy shop that Joey and Chandler have been after.

Ross and Rachel have been fighting for the group's attention since the breakup. Rachel invites everyone except Ross to her family cabin in the mountains, but on the way to the cabin, they run out of petrol. Everyone wants to call Ross for help, but Rachel won't let them.

Phoebe is upset when her 18-year-old half-brother, Frank Jr, wants to marry his attractive home economics teacher, who is more than 25 years older than him. Elsewhere, Monica receives a tip from an admirer worth a small fortune, and a hypnosis tape intended to assist Chandler give up smoking has a rather strange effect on him.

Rachel's former colleague Mark asks her out on a date. When Rachel invites Ross to her apartment, he thinks she wants to get back together, but she just wants to return his things. Later, as Rachel and Mark return from their date, Ross spies on them through the peephole of Joey and Chandler's door. Meanwhile, Monica dates a millionaire, and Joey is cast in a play and clashes with the female lead.

Monica inherits a beautiful dollhouse that is too elaborate to play with, so Phoebe makes her own, but it meets a sad end. Meanwhile, Joey thinks he's found his true love, and Rachel's boss dates Chandler, placing her in a dangerous situation.
BAFTA award-winning comedian Michael McIntyre returns with a brand-new episode of his big show, featuring Shirley Ballas, Judi Love and music from Ball & Boe.
Michael McIntyre hosts as Chris McCausland, Gabby Logan, GK Barry, Iain Stirling, Liza Tarbuck, Rachel Riley and Trevor Nelson try to help the contestants answer their way to a fortune.
The team are joined by actress Marisol Nichols and guest comic Jonathan Mangum as they play classics Weird Newscasters, Duet, and Props.
Jimmy Carr, GK Barry and Jamali Maddix are seeking out a****** behaviour. There's a woman who lied about a dog's ashes and someone who believes they're the reincarnation of Princess Diana.
Reliving the most compelling court cases, past and present, that have captured the nation's attention, through top-notch storytelling and the use of archival footage from the Court TV vaults.

Emotions ran high in the days following the 9/11 attack on the United States. For the most part, the grief and anger brought people together, but for Frank Roque, it was a motivation for killing an innocent immigrant chasing the American dream.
Timothy Ring and his crew planned the perfect crime, robbing an armoured car outside a mall on one of America's busiest shopping days. But after the heist, they never planned how to get away with it.
Live gavel-to-gavel coverage, in-depth legal reporting and expert analysis of America's most important and compelling trials.
Shanda Vander Ark, a promising law clerk, faces murder charges in the death of her own child.
Vinnie Politan takes a deep dive into the true-crime stories that are captivating the world over, featuring sharp analysis and insightful interviews for a deeper understanding of these cases.
When Falonda Simpson and her daughter Davonda Washington are found murdered, investigators realise the culprit may be very close to home.
After a mysterious motorcycle rider stalks and shoots down a Tulsa man, detectives must piece together the events leading up to his death to find out who wanted him dead and why.

Lieutenant Joe Kenda finds the bullet-ridden bodies of a middle-aged couple in a musty suburban house alongside the corpses of their two beloved pets. Detectives discover an essential clue hidden behind a birdcage.
Kenda and Barry investigate a gun battle in a quaint family home that left one dead and two in critical condition; a woman is found beaten, strangled and stabbed on the roadside.

A wanted felon smashes into a state trooper's car while fleeing from local police and county deputies; police get into a shootout with a man wanted for murdering his roommate; a deputy's PIT manoeuvre knocks a fugitive's car up on two wheels.
A woman alerts police to a crime she's committing, a golf game leads to one player to see red on the green, a man wants to get paid by police during a traffic stop, and more.

A man with a late-night urge to relieve himself picks an unusual spot to go; a fugitive leads police on a wild foot chase down the middle of a busy motorway; a woman involved in a fender bender has an over-the-top reaction.
A convicted drug dealer makes a daring courthouse escape after sentencing; a woman convicted of Felony D.U.I. and Reckless Homicide makes an emotional courtroom apology to the victim's family.

Jody Dobrowski was just 24 when he was brutally murdered in an attack so cruel, he could only be identified through fingerprints. His attackers were motivated by homophobic thuggery and planned an attack based solely on sexuality.

On 11 May 2006, Nisha Patel-Nasri was upstairs getting ready for bed when she heard the front door open. She grabbed a torch and went to confront the intruder. She was stabbed in the thigh with a John Lewis knife from her kitchen.
Dean Mayley had learning difficulties and was taking steps in becoming an independent adult. On his way home he encountered a group of men who taunted him and beat him to death.
When Patrick De La Cerda is shot and killed on his own doorstep, his fiancée Jessica suggests a jealous ex-boyfriend may be behind the attack.

A beloved grandmother is found with a red bathrobe sash knotted around her neck. Her death appears to be a suicide until the medical examiner rules homicide; the victim's husband is charged with murder, but the case takes a surprising turn.

A car crash on a rural highway leaves one woman dead while her husband walks away unscathed; it appears to be a tragic accident, but one state trooper can't shake the feeling the crash is anything but routine.

Firefighters discover the charred remains of a young wife and mother, but the flames didn't kill her; she sustained a gunshot wound to the head, and the evidence points to her taking her own life; loved ones argue it's a case of murder.

A man suing his former employer enrages a judge by using an AI-generated character to argue his case; an inmate at the county jail who claims she can't afford her $5,000 bond asks the judge if she can go back to her cell and go to sleep; and more.

A convicted felon tries to escape while being ushered back to jail; the judge changes a defendant's sentence after she catches him lying in court; a man accused of indecent exposure is held in contempt after swearing at the judge; and more.

A look at some of the strangest arrests from across the country. A shopper on gummies freaks out at the supermarket, a man drives backwards on a major thoroughfare, and a car smashes through a fast-food restaurant.

A look at some of the strangest arrests from across the country. A man dangles precariously from a bridge trying to elude police, two women are arrested for twerking on a police car with the officer still inside, and a man calls police on a stripper.

During Alaska's summer solstice, Alaska State Troopers confront a fleeing suspect, defuse an armed barricade and investigate arson near the Arctic Circle. One wild night of endless daylight tests the limits of law in the Last Frontier.
News and commentary about current events and issues facing the world in a spirit of faith.
A church service including praise and worship and an inspiring message by Pastor Mac Hammond.
'Healing Miracles' showcases the healing power of Jesus Christ with Addison Adamu by exploring various healing testimonies and miracles from people of all walks of life.
As a cardiologist, evangelist, medical missionary, and author, Samuel Kojoglanian serves the Lord and mankind in the name of Jesus and the power of the Holy Spirit.
Kenneth Copeland Ministries is a teaching ministry assigned by God to preach the gospel of Jesus Christ all around the world and without compromise in order to get the message out that Jesus is Lord.
Equipping Pastors, group leaders and church members with biblical truth and tools to heal themselves and take healing to a wounded world.
Joni and guests tackle a wide range of relevant issues, controversial subjects and hard-hitting news topics with candour and wit.
Delivering hope and reassurance for the troubled times we live in, hosted by the Lamb family and featuring interviews with leading voices on a variety of subjects.
Familiar hymns and beautifully produced original music accompany Scripture to help you let go and surrender during a time of daily prayer and meditation.
Host Nancy Dufresne shares messages addressing the topics of faith, healing, renewing the mind, following the Holy Spirit and a life in Christ.
Free Chapel pastor, Jentezen Franklin, shares his interpretation of the Bible by bringing practical meaning to spiritual truths in a contemporary world.
Joseph Z provides prophetic commentary on global events through faith-based journalism and teaching.
Messages from author and evangelist Joel Osteen as he preaches of love and hope. The pastor urges people to live to their full potential and form a close relationship with God.
The author and speaker recounts his battle with cancer and the natural treatments he elected to undergo in lieu of chemotherapy.
Rabbi Jonathan Bernis of Jewish Voice Ministries shares the lessons he learned after his miraculous health recovery.

Dr. Creflo Dollar ministers to all walks of life with hope for change. With a renewal of faith, mind, and spirit, he and his wife Taffi share their vision for all to understand God's love and promises.
Renowned Christian scholar Rick Renner delves into the Greek New Testament, blending historical texts with modern illustrations to unpack God's message for His believers.
Join believers from across the nation and the continent as Pastor Benny Hinn ministers God's power, bringing healing, deliverance, and revival.
Real-life solutions and Biblical insight on topics of finances, family, and faith: from author, speaker and pastor Gary Keesee.
John Ankerberg, a Baptist minister, spreads the message of Jesus Christ among the followers and urges them to live a more spiritual life.

Messianic investigator Sid Roth discusses and examines the supernatural reality and power of God, and includes testimonies from those who have experienced extraordinary healings, miracles, and personal encounters with God.

Biblical teaching, inspirational guests, encouragement and classic messages from Marilyn Hickey meant to strengthen faith, inspire hope and help viewers experience the transforming power of God's Word in everyday life.

David Dickinson and a team of antiques dealers visit Colwyn Bay, to give locals a chance to put their valuables into auction or accept a cash sum. Helen Gardiner finds out that sealing a deal for a collection of 1950s Dinky toys is far from child's play; Karen Dalmeny duels it out for a commemorative sword and Corrie Jeffrey's enticed by an eighteenth-century snuff box that's not to be sniffed at.

Seth's security crackdown rubs the redeem girls the wrong way, and American Jewellery comes up short-staffed, forcing the Golds to man the windows. Out of his element, Seth struggles to stay on the ball.

Seth and Ashley battle it out to see who can bring in more new customers to the store. Ashley's idea really blows up, but Seth has a secret plan in the works, and one that might just push his sister over the edge, and out of American Jewelry.

Customer drama is nothing new to the Golds, but when uproar in the pawn line reveals that an employee may be taking bribes, Ashley vows to get to the bottom of things, Les and Seth brush off her conspiracy theory.

With employee relations not his strong suit, Seth tries to make amends by moving staff around, but his plan backfires when his swap leads to a staff throw down and Les checks out an old school peep show.
Seth is shocked when Les brings back ex-pawn shop employee Amy. He later spots a mistake that could cost the store thousands of dollars.

Les buys rare rock memorabilia that may be worth a pile of cash. Then, when a man gets caught trying to secretly sell his girlfriend's ring, she dishes out a punishment that's never been seen in the store before.

A couple attempts to return a supposedly mint-condition video game that has since malfunctioned. Meanwhile, a female customer accuses the shop of replacing the stones in her pawned jewellery when speaking to Ashley.
Les ignores Ashley's cries to up security after she finds a potential robber hiding in the shop fridge. It's a move he may regret come nightfall.
Despite the storeroom being packed to the rafters, Les cannot resist buying more. At risk of being labelled a hoarder, he faces mounting pressure to boost sales.
Les gets excited over a jar of powdered gold. An explosive acid test reveals if it is worth thousands, or if it is just eyeshadow.
The shop lands itself in trouble when a customer calls in their lawyer to settle a huge row over a fake receipt. Fortunately, Les has a trick up his sleeve.
Ashley sets up an unusual contest against Seth in the pawn shop. If Seth loses, his closely guarded secret will be revealed to everyone.
Les loses his temper when the kids suggest he sells their failing second store. With the family's livelihood at stake, Seth puts a sneaky plan into action.
Ashley is pulled into the fray as Seth's plan to sell the Pontiac shop hits a snag. Then a meeting with a buyer leaves them in a life-changing situation.
After Seth attempted to sell his father's business out from under him, Les cannot forgive or forget his son's betrayal. The remaining employees puzzle over what might have happened.
The Golds acquire a potentially rare guitar but struggle to determine its authenticity. Meanwhile, Ashley finds herself at loggerheads with a challenging customer.

With their father-son relationship already on the rocks, a major miscommunication between Les and Seth could land a key employee on the chopping block. Ashley tries to keep the peace, but the damage may be too deep.
When Les allows a $60,000 watch to walk out the door on a handshake agreement, Seth and Ashley flip out. A life-sized Silver Surfer slides into the shop, and Didgeridoo leaves the staff breathless.

In the wake of Les' bum watch deal, Seth and Ashley get on his case to curb his crazy buys. He makes a deal to get the kids off his back, but when some interesting animals come through the door, it might be too much for Les to resist.
Les has finally heard enough from Seth and Ashley about his bum watch band deal and bets that he can sell them off just to get the kids off his back and Ashley turns barber for a day.

Following the quirky day-to-day operations of American Jewelry and Loan, a family-owned and operated pawn shop in Detroit, Michigan. This time, Seth and Ashley start the day with a wager that leaves one of them dressed to the nines.

Ashley is livid when she gets cut out of a deal by Les and Seth. Trying to keep the peace and the business running smoothly, Les separates the siblings, but the battle spills onto the sales floor in a huge way.
The sibling rivalry between Seth and Ashley is at an all-time high and when Ashley faces down not one, but two baseball deals that are clearly outside her comfort zone, Seth cries foul.
Brawling isn't exactly out of the ordinary at American Jewelry and Loan, but when customers start throwing down in the car park before the doors even open, Les knows it's a bad sign.
Skipton is the location today as Cheryl Hakeney gets herself in a spin over an Art Deco bronze figure, other items brought along include a Royal Doulton Toby jug, and a cavalier sword.
Burton-on-Trent is the location today as a naive marine painting comes through the door, and there are some saucy postcards that make Jo Brayshaw chuckle.

David Dickinson is joined by Tim Hogarth, Cheryl Hakeney, David Hakeney and Alison Chapman. A blunderbuss that is rumoured to be linked to Captain Kidd washes up in the den, along with another item from a Chinese shipwreck and a beautiful inkwell.

David Dickinson and his team of antique dealers are in Morecambe where a condiment set with a famous name attached to it turns up on Cheryl Hakeney's table but will she realise? Alison Chapman surprises the owner of a Japanese vase and a riot ensues on Tim Hogarth's table when a colourful seller brings in their gold.
